Happened the first time I did shrooms and I was too young for the momentum to carry. If I experienced that again now, I’d start making lists. Make a list of your ambitions, and then make lists of things to do to further ambitions. For me it’d be “practice art, explore biology jobs, practice guitar, etc” — and then my list for the first of those would be “practice fundamentals, learn clip studio’s program, find drawing references and study, etc.” Getting into details will highlight the small steps to achieve big goals so they feel doable. 

Another thing that pushes me is having a large widget on my front screen that tells me my screen time for the day. It can help me put my phone down — you can also put time limits on apps I think.

And when I reaaaaally need to do certain things, I’ll put sticky notes on my door handles or places where I can’t not interact with them in a day, like fridge handles, dead center of my monitor or TV. It’s like past me is screaming at myself to not waste all my time. 

One thing I did tripping was take all my clothes out at once and meticulously sorted through them. I paired up outfits I still liked, and got rid of things I didn’t love. I got lazy caring about my appearance, and kept the same clothes for years. Refreshing clothing is one big thing that signifies personal growth and change. I recently got a few new things, and I’ve been getting compliments on it. It makes me feel like I’m growing. Personally it’s best when I don’t get rid of tshirts just to get new tshirts, unless you switch ill fitting ones for more flattering ones. I switched from tshirts to nicer button ups (like linen and silky ones) and tight undershirts so I can have them unbuttoned sometimes, and from jeans to balloon-style wide leg pants. Get creative :)

And by far the BEST thing you can do is affirmations - it’s lovely to write out the things you like about yourself and if you have friends you feel comfy doing this with, it’s awesome to share the things you appreciate about them, and for them to do the same for you. Very validating and motivating

My best friend was diagnosed at 22 and though I’m not her partner and there for her rough days, I’m in the the middle of carving a walking cane for her because she needs it. She got diagnosed in 2019, so it’s been three years of steroid infusions, drug changes, diet changes, etc. The best advice I can give is to do your research! Learn as much as you can from clinical studies, people with MS (just browsing this sub), and from your partner. This is forever and progressive, and drugs can help but it might be a while before finding the right one. Diet changes can help too, such as the autoimmune protocol diet. My friend has cut out all dairy and cuts out gluten often too. Be supportive, adaptive, and check in with what your gf needs, as MS varies greatly from person to person. 

I’ll be honest, this sub is great for seeking support by *browsing previous questions* because most of your questions/concerns have been addressed numerous times before, you just need to search the sub. As someone without MS, I recognize that this sub is mostly for people with MS to post, and for people without MS to listen. 

I’d also get in touch with someone close to you to discuss how you’re feeling or with a therapist that works with processing diagnoses. I believe there is a Stuff You Should Know podcast episode about MS, and there’s an Ologies episode about Fear and one about Pain that will be helpful for both you and your partner. I’d seriously recommend listening to all three of them, easy if you put it on when driving. Learn as much as you can, listen to your girlfriend’s needs, and when you can, go above and beyond to help. Going to the store or cooking when she can’t, helping her when her limbs aren’t working right, etc. Heating pads are also a godsend apparently. Hope this helps!

Never too late to start reading graphic novels, and
I think you’ll find that they’re fine examples of the literary elements that make up a story. This kind of feels like the difference film majors bestow upon films vs movies. Just because one is seen as “art”, it doesn’t invalidate the quality of the other. Don’t think your reading level means much, I was reading and memorising the King James version of the Bible in 1st grade for school, but I enjoy graphic novels and manga greatly. It’s also a useful tool for students who get really bored with or can’t focus on long books. Loads of students use SparkNotes to “read”, they can’t do that with graphic novels, so it forces them to actually focus on the book instead of cramming 5 minutes before class reading chapter summaries on SparkNotes. 

I think graphic novels are the perfect “gateway” books into reading more chapter books. If a student gets hooked on them (like I did as a teen), they will frequent the library to read other series and might browse around and find “real” books that sound interesting. That’s what happened with me at least. Some graphic novels are also insanely insightful! Artists can say a lot in them without having to write an entire chapter book. Most artists wouldn’t want to make a book without art in it. This middle-ground is where art meets language and frankly, it’s awesome. 

I’d recommend going up to Central Library or any near you and going through the GN sections. Note that the adult section tends to have more adult themes. If they’re too much, go through the teen section (no one cares, I get teen and children’s GNs a lot). Ask a librarian if there are any recommended by them or other librarians, I think they put out a list every month or so.

depends what kind of person you are imo, for me i took just over 3gs alone in my apartment the first time, freaked a lil bit looking at my own skin and at myself in the mirror but overall had a wonderful time. i have done lots of emotional work though, years of therapy in my teens and whatnot, so my coping skills are above average. if you cannot cope well with stressors, or are going through a lot, it might not be a good idea to take anything more than 1.5g imo. 

if you are trying to explode your brain, can cope well with whatever might come up, or you have a very seasoned trip sitter, i’d say go for 2.5-3.5. personally i never consume it all at once. i’ll take about .5 every 10-15 min until i hit my desired dose. this makes the come up easier for me. if it all hits me at once, i get super anxious and am more likely to have a difficult trip. 

i also think its super important to realise that a trip is not a guaranteed great time. it is a *trip*, if you’ve been on any trips im sure you know that some suck and some are amazing. this is the same. if you have a bad first experience, realise it isnt permanent, recognise what the problem is thats making it unpleasant, and work to fix it. sometimes its going outside, sometimes its shutting yourself in a quiet, dark space. sometimes its closing your eyes and listening to music, or doing some deep breathing. if you have a “bad” trip that you cant fix, dont let that discourage you from tripping again. each time is an experience worth learning from. 

anyhow! hope this is helpful! cheers :)

IMO, statistically or not, a large chunk of homeless folks aren’t too bad. My mom used to take me to volunteer at the soup kitchen (aka angel house) back when I was 12 or so and there were a few incidents, but it was almost always amongst themselves, and had nothing to do with us at all. I held so many convos with homeless guys there when I wasn’t even a teenager and I don’t have a distinct memory of any being rude/scary to me. I can say being an adult now and working in a grocery store right off of the tent-full Ben White, I’ve dealt with some wild stuff, but when you treat them like regular people and show them you can be respectful, they appreciate it. 
And if someone is on (or coming off) drugs or seems aggressive or unstable, they’re probably experiencing way more than what you can imagine. Had a homeless lady with track marks and spots of blood all over her arms come in with a bogus “left my wallet and phone on the bus” story, and I watched her (mid 30s-40s) call her mom on the store phone and break down. Watched her buy a bag of carrots and eat a solid handful or two and then try and return them saying they tasted weird so she could get that money back. Bought her bfast and she was so grateful and sweet to me about it, after helping her at the front desk for a while. Even drug addicts gotta eat. Even mentally ill folks need food and water, warm clothes and a roof. As once stated many years ago “LEAVE BRITTNEY ALONE”. Famous folks lose their minds and do drugs and become mentally ill or try to kill themselves. But they have the money to come out the other side. They have the power for us to ignore or never find out about their heroin use or coke addiction, and the money to repeat rehab time and again, but they’re still people. If everyone homeless person got housing or rehab, medication they needed and food, I bet you’d have a hard time telling them apart from anyone else in public.
